result:
If I could change one thing about the world, I would give everyone a genuine, shared sense of empathy—an ability to feel and understand the joys, fears, and burdens of another human as if they were my own.  

It isn’t a quick fix; it’s a deep, cultural shift that would ripple through every policy, law, conversation, and creative expression. With that kind of connection, disputes would be approached as collaborative problems rather than zero‑sum battles, medical aid would reach even the most remote corners, and environmental stewardship would feel like a communal promise rather than a distant obligation.  

Empathy has the power to dissolve the divisions that keep us far apart. If we all could tilt our worldview from “me versus you” to “we together,” the other urgent needs—poverty, inequality, climate change—would become far more solvable, because we would see the real cost of neglect in the eyes of those we’re meant to help.
